name: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation

criteria.description: No evidence of structural heart disease on imaging and autopsy
Documented episode(s) of ventricular fibrillation or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Exclusion of other known causes of ventricular fibrillation including ischemic heart disease, cardiomyopathies, channelopathies, and electrolyte abnormalities
Family history of sudden cardiac death or unexplained syncope may be supportive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of documented ventricular fibrillation with no identifiable structural heart disease or other known causes after comprehensive evaluation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is one of exclusion and requires thorough cardiac evaluation including imaging, electrophysiological studies, and genetic testing when indicated.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sudden cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation
searchTerms: unexpected cardiac arrest with irregular heartbeat
heart suddenly stops due to ventricular fibrillation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Syncope caused by transient ventricular fibrillation episodes
searchTerms: syncope caused by heart rhythm problems
nocturnal choking or struggling to breathe
fatigue due to heart rhythm problems
palpitations not linked to irregular heartbeat
feeling heart beat fast without rhythm issues
nighttime seizures that look like epilepsy

rare.symptomName: Sudden unexplained death in family members
searchTerms: family history of sudden unexplained death
temporary blurred vision with irregular heartbeat
visual disturbances linked to heart rhythm

laboratory: Normal cardiac biomarkers in absence of ischemia
imaging: Normal echocardiogram with no structural abnormalities
other: Electrophysiological study showing inducible ventricular fibrillation
Exclusion of ischemic heart disease by coronary angiography or CT

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic ECG pattern with coved ST elevation in V1-V3
Family history of sudden cardiac death
Genetic mutations in SCN5A more commonly identified
Syncope triggered by exercise or stress
Genetic mutations affecting potassium or sodium channels
Structural abnormalities of right ventricle on imaging
Ventricular arrhythmias originating from right ventricle

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest without prior warning
Family history of sudden unexplained death
references: Priori SG, et al. 2015 ESC Guidelines for the management of patients with ventricular arrhythmias and the prevention of sudden cardiac death. Eur Heart J. 2015.
